## N26 Products and Account Features

N26, the German digital bank founded in 2013 and headquartered in Berlin, offers a comprehensive range of products and account features across multiple tiers and has recently expanded its product portfolio significantly.

---

### Account Tiers

#### 1. **N26 Standard** (Free)
- No opening or maintenance fees
- Virtual Mastercard debit card (usable via Apple Pay and Google Pay)
- SEPA Instant Credit transfers at no extra cost
- Real-time spending notifications
- Basic budgeting and finance management tools

#### 2. **N26 Smart** (€4.90/month)
- Physical Mastercard debit card (choice of five colors)
- Up to 6 virtual cards
- 3 free domestic ATM withdrawals per month
- Up to 10 **Spaces** sub-accounts (with their own IBANs) for budgeting, savings goals, and direct debits
- **Shared Spaces** — manage funds together with up to 10 other N26 customers
- Link a virtual card to a Space to spend directly from it
- **Instant Savings** account with flexible access
- Automatic **Rules** to sort money into sub-accounts
- Round-ups and Income Sorter features

#### 3. **N26 Go** (€9.90/month)
- All Smart features, plus:
- **Travel insurance** (provided by Allianz) — covers trip cancellation, trip interruption, travel delay, baggage delay/loss, emergency medical & transportation, and personal liability while travelling (up to €10,000 for cancellation/rebooking fees)
- No foreign transaction fees on payments abroad
- Free international ATM withdrawals
- 5 free trades per month for Stocks & ETFs

#### 4. **N26 Metal** (€16.90/month)
- All Go features, plus:
- Premium heavyweight **metal card** in multiple colors/finishes
- Enhanced travel insurance (including pandemic/epidemic coverage via Allianz), mobile phone protection, and purchase protection
- Coverage extends to spouse/cohabitant and children (up to age 25 if in education) for travel covers
- Personal liability while travelling up to €500,000
- Unlimited free ATM withdrawals worldwide
- No markup on foreign exchange rates for card purchases and withdrawals
- 10 free trades per month for Stocks & ETFs
- Up to **4% interest** on Instant Savings
- Priority customer support
- Exclusive partner offers

---

### Business Accounts

N26 offers **Business Standard**, **Business Smart**, **Business Go**, and **Business Metal** accounts for freelancers and self-employed individuals, mirroring the personal tiers with added business features such as:
- 0.1% cashback on card purchases (Business Go)
- Automatic transaction categorization via AI
- Free monthly stock/ETF trades (Business Go and Business Metal)
- Accounting and invoicing tools (in development)
- A new **Small & Medium Business account** is also being rolled out for companies (sole proprietorships, UG, GmbH, AG) with up to 9 employees and max €2 million annual turnover, offering up to 0.5% cashback and free eurozone ATM withdrawals

---

### Key Features Across All Accounts

| Feature | Details |
|---|---|
| **Stocks & ETFs** | Buy and sell 4,000+ stocks, ETFs, and ETCs directly in the app for a flat €0.90 per trade (powered by Upvest). Fractional investing and savings plans available. Free trades included with Go (3/month), Metal (10/month). |
| **Crypto** | Crypto portfolio management within the app |
| **Instant Savings** | Flexible savings account with interest; rates vary by tier (up to 4% for Metal) |
| **Spaces** | Sub-accounts with individual IBANs for budgeting and goal-setting (up to 10 with Smart and above) |
| **Joint Accounts** | Shared account functionality |
| **Real-time notifications** | Push alerts for every transaction |
| **Mobile payments** | Apple Pay and Google Pay support |
| **SEPA transfers** | Instant incoming SEPA Credit transfers at no extra cost |
| **International transfers** | Send money abroad from the app |
| **Security** | Mastercard SecureCode, biometric login, card lock/unlock in-app |

---

### New Products and Features Launched in 2024-2025

#### **2024 Launches:**

1. **N26 Stocks & ETFs (January 2024)**
   - Launched in partnership with Upvest
   - Customers can buy and sell fractional shares of European and US assets at a fixed fee of €0.90 per trade
   - Initially rolled out in Austria, then expanded to Germany, Ireland, and other markets
   - Offers over 500 European and US stocks
   - Fee-free savings plans introduced
   - Free monthly trades for N26 You and N26 Metal members
   - Access to free Investment Plans

2. **N26 Crypto — France (March 2024)**
   - Launched cryptocurrency trading product in France
   - Allows customers to trade over 200 cryptocurrencies directly in the N26 app
   - Developed in partnership with Bitpanda GmbH
   - N26 Metal customers benefit from lower transaction fees (1% on Bitcoin, 2% on other coins)
   - Standard customers pay 1.5% on Bitcoin and 2.5% on other coins

3. **N26 Crypto — Germany, Switzerland, Belgium, Portugal & Ireland (2024)**
   - Expanded crypto trading to additional European markets
   - Offers nearly 200 coins
   - Same tiered pricing structure as France launch

4. **Updated Insurance Services (2024)**
   - Enhanced insurance for 'You' and 'Metal' personal and business account holders
   - Travel delays now covered after just 2 hours (down from 4)
   - Baggage delays covered after 4 hours (down from 12)
   - Personal liability coverage increased to €500,000 per trip
   - Coverage still includes baggage and travel delays up to €500, baggage theft up to €2,000, medical emergencies up to €1 million, and trip cancellations/interruptions up to €10,000

5. **N26 Instant Savings — Spain**
   - Launched Instant Savings account in Spain
   - Offers Spanish IBAN with 2.26% AER on deposits
   - No minimum deposit required
   - No conditions of permanence
   - No additional fees
   - Maximum balance of €50,000 for earning interest

6. **Instant Savings Expansion to 13 European Countries**
   - Extended instant savings accounts to 13 European countries
   - Broadened access to interest-bearing savings across customer base

#### **2025 Performance:**

- N26 reached its first full-year net profit in 2025 (€1.6 million net income)
- Revenue grew 13% to €501.6 million (from €445.4 million in 2024)
- Fee and commission income grew 21% to €184.2 million
- Net interest income grew 49% to €166.3 million
- Processes over €140 billion in transactions annually
- Serves customers in 24 European markets

---

N26's product strategy in 2024-2025 focused on transforming from a pure digital bank into a broader financial platform, adding investing (stocks, ETFs), crypto trading, enhanced insurance, and competitive savings products — all integrated within a single mobile app.

claims.text: N26 is a German fintech and digital bank headquartered in Berlin, founded in 2013.

N26 Standard is a free account with no opening or maintenance fees, offering a virtual Mastercard debit card usable via Apple Pay and Google Pay, SEPA Instant Credit transfers at no extra cost, real-time spending notifications, and basic budgeting tools.

N26 Smart costs €4.90 per month and includes a physical Mastercard debit card in five colors, up to 6 virtual cards, 3 free domestic ATM withdrawals per month, up to 10 Spaces sub-accounts with IBANs, Shared Spaces, Instant Savings account, automatic Rules, round-ups, and Income Sorter features.

N26 Go costs €9.90 per month and includes all Smart features plus travel insurance provided by Allianz covering trip cancellation, interruption, delays, baggage issues, emergency medical and personal liability up to €10,000, no foreign transaction fees, free international ATM withdrawals, and 5 free trades per month for Stocks & ETFs.

N26 Metal costs €16.90 per month and includes all Go features plus a premium metal card, enhanced travel insurance with pandemic coverage, mobile phone and purchase protection, coverage for spouse/cohabitant and children up to age 25, personal liability up to €500,000, unlimited free ATM withdrawals worldwide, no FX markup, 10 free trades per month for Stocks & ETFs, up to 4% interest on Instant Savings, and priority customer support.

N26 offers Business Standard, Business Smart, Business Go, and Business Metal accounts with features including 0.1% cashback on card purchases, automatic AI transaction categorization, free monthly stock/ETF trades, and accounting/invoicing tools in development.
A new Small & Medium Business account is being rolled out for companies with up to 9 employees and max €2 million annual turnover, offering up to 0.5% cashback and free eurozone ATM withdrawals.

N26 offers Stocks & ETFs trading for 4,000+ stocks, ETFs, and ETCs at €0.90 per trade powered by Upvest, with fractional investing and savings plans available, and free trades for Go (3/month) and Metal (10/month) members.

N26 launched Stocks & ETFs trading in January 2024 in partnership with Upvest, initially in Austria, then expanded to Germany, Ireland, and other markets, offering over 500 European and US stocks with fee-free savings plans.

N26 launched N26 Crypto in France in March 2024, allowing customers to trade over 200 cryptocurrencies in partnership with Bitpanda GmbH, with Metal customers paying 1% on Bitcoin and 2% on other coins, while standard customers pay 1.5% on Bitcoin and 2.5% on other coins.
N26 Crypto expanded to Germany, Switzerland, Belgium, Portugal, and Ireland in 2024, offering nearly 200 coins with the same tiered pricing structure.

N26 updated insurance services in 2024 for You and Metal account holders, reducing travel delay coverage to 2 hours (from 4), baggage delay to 4 hours (from 12), and increasing personal liability coverage to €500,000 per trip, while maintaining coverage for baggage/travel delays up to €500, baggage theft up to €2,000, medical emergencies up to €1 million, and trip cancellations/interruptions up to €10,000.

N26 launched Instant Savings in Spain with a Spanish IBAN offering 2.26% AER on deposits, no minimum deposit, no conditions of permanence, no additional fees, and a maximum balance of €50,000 for earning interest.
N26 extended Instant Savings accounts to 13 European countries in 2024.

N26 reached its first full-year net profit in 2025 with €1.6 million net income on €501.6 million revenue (13% growth from €445.4 million in 2024), with fee and commission income growing 21% to €184.2 million and net interest income growing 49% to €166.3 million.
N26 processes over €140 billion in transactions annually and serves customers in 24 European markets.

answer:
## Revolut Plans, Prices, and Fee Structure by Tier

Revolut offers **five personal account tiers** with escalating benefits structured as lifestyle memberships. Here's a comprehensive breakdown of each tier's pricing and how fees differ:

---

### **1. Standard — FREE**
- **Monthly price:** £0
- **Physical debit card:** £4.99
- **Currency exchange:**
  - Fee-free up to £1,000/month (weekdays only)
  - 1% fee on weekend exchanges
- **ATM withdrawals:** Fee-free up to €200/month (or 5 withdrawals, whichever comes first)
- **Stock trading:** 1 commission-free trade per month
- **Additional trade commission:** 0.25%
- **Custody fee:** 0.12% per annum
- **Basic features:** Money management, budgeting tools, international transfers

---

### **2. Plus — £3.99/month (or £40/year)**
- **Currency exchange:**
  - Fee-free up to £3,000/month
  - 0.5% weekend FX fee (reduced from Standard's 1%)
- **ATM withdrawals:** Fee-free up to €200/month
- **Stock trading:** 3 commission-free trades per month
- **Additional trade commission:** 0.25%
- **Custody fee:** 0.12% per annum
- **Additional benefits:** Purchase insurance, disposable virtual cards, Junior accounts

---

### **3. Premium — £7.99/month (or £80/year)**
- **Currency exchange:**
  - **Unlimited** fee-free currency exchange
  - **No weekend surcharge** (0% weekend FX fee)
- **ATM withdrawals:** Fee-free up to €400/month
- **Stock trading:** 5 commission-free trades per month
- **Additional trade commission:** 0.25%
- **Custody fee:** 0.12% per annum
- **Additional benefits:** Travel insurance, access to lifestyle partner subscriptions (Deliveroo, Tinder), better savings rates

---

### **4. Metal — £14.99/month (or £140/year)**
- **Currency exchange:**
  - **Unlimited** fee-free currency exchange
  - **No weekend surcharge**
- **ATM withdrawals:** Fee-free up to €800/month
- **Stock trading:** 10 commission-free trades per month
- **Additional trade commission:** 0.25%
- **Custody fee:** 0.12% per annum
- **Exclusive features:**
  - Stainless-steel card
  - Enhanced travel insurance and purchase protection
  - Car hire excess cover
  - Cashback on card payments
  - Broader partner subscriptions (Financial Times, ClassPass, etc.)
  - **Total subscription value:** ~£2,200/year

---

### **5. Ultra — £55/month**
- **Currency exchange:**
  - **Unlimited** fee-free currency exchange
  - **No weekend surcharge**
- **ATM withdrawals:** Fee-free up to €2,000/month
- **Stock trading:** 10 commission-free trades per month
- **Additional trade commission:** **0.12%** (reduced from 0.25% on other plans)
- **Custody fee:** 0.12% per annum
- **Savings rate:** Up to 4% AER (variable)
- **Premium features:**
  - Unlimited airport lounge access
  - 3 GB monthly global data roaming in 100+ countries
  - Extensive partner subscriptions: Financial Times Premium Digital, WeWork, MasterClass Full, Uber One, NordVPN Complete, Headspace, Sleep Cycle Premium, Freeletics, Picsart Gold, The Athletic, ClassPass, Perplexity Pro, Chess.com, Headway Premium, Tinder Gold, Turo
  - Comprehensive insurance including cancellation cover
  - **Total benefits valued:** Over £4,000/year

---

## **Key Fee Differences Across Tiers**

| **Fee Type** | **Standard** | **Plus** | **Premium** | **Metal** | **Ultra** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Monthly price** | Free | £3.99 | £7.99 | £14.99 | £55 |
| **Weekend FX fee** | 1% | 0.5% | None | None | None |
| **Weekday FX fair-use limit** | £1,000/mo | £3,000/mo | Unlimited | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| **Fee-free ATM withdrawals** | €200/mo | €200/mo | €400/mo | €800/mo | Up to €2,000/mo |
| **Commission-free trades** | 1/mo | 3/mo | 5/mo | 10/mo | 10/mo |
| **Extra trade commission** | 0.25% | 0.25% | 0.25% | 0.25% | 0.12% |
| **Custody fee (investments)** | 0.12% p.a. | 0.12% p.a. | 0.12% p.a. | 0.12% p.a. | 0.12% p.a. |

**Note:** Beyond ATM free limits, a 2% fee applies (minimum €1 per withdrawal).

---

## **US-Specific Pricing**

Revolut offers **three tiers** in the United States (as of early 2026):
- **Standard:** $0/month
- **Premium:** $9.99/month
- **Metal:** $16.99/month

US Standard customers receive:
- Up to $1,200/month in fee-free out-of-network ATM withdrawals
- 10 free international remittances per month
- Up to $200,000/month in commission-free crypto trading

---

## **Upcoming Price Changes (Europe — Effective July 2026)**

Revolut has announced price increases for European markets (e.g., Portugal):
- **Premium:** Rising ~10% (e.g., €10.39 → €11.43/month)
- **Metal:** Rising ~12.4% (e.g., €16.63 → €18.70/month)
- **Ultra:** Rising ~9% (e.g., €57.20 → €62.40/month)
- **Plus** (€4.15) and **Standard** remain unchanged

Customers must decide before July 2026; silence will be treated as consent to the new rates.

---

## **Summary of Key Tier Differences**

The main differentiators across tiers are:

1. **Currency exchange limits and weekend fees:** Standard and Plus have monthly limits and weekend fees, while Premium, Metal, and Ultra offer unlimited fee-free exchange with no weekend surcharges.

2. **ATM withdrawal limits:** Progressively increase from €200/month (Standard/Plus) to €2,000/month (Ultra).

3. **Stock trading allowances:** Range from 1 free trade/month (Standard) to 10 free trades/month (Metal/Ultra), with Ultra offering a lower commission rate (0.12% vs 0.25%) on additional trades.

4. **Lifestyle benefits:** Higher tiers include travel insurance, partner subscriptions, cashback, airport lounge access, and global data roaming, with total benefit values ranging from £2,200/year (Metal) to over £4,000/year (Ultra).

5. **Savings rates:** Ultra offers the highest savings rate at up to 4% AER (variable).

## Revolut Subscription Plans, Pricing & Fees

Revolut offers five personal account tiers — one free and four paid — structured as lifestyle memberships with escalating benefits.

---

### 1. Standard — **Free**
- Basic money management, budgeting tools, and international transfers.
- Fee-free currency exchange up to £1,000/month (weekdays only; 1% fee at weekends).
- Fee-free ATM withdrawals up to €200/month (or 5 withdrawals, whichever comes first).
- 1 commission-free stock trade per month.
- Physical debit card costs £4.99.

### 2. Plus — **£3.99/month** (or £40/year)
- Better spending-abroad limits; 0.5% weekend FX fee (reduced from 1%).
- Fee-free currency exchange up to £3,000/month.
- Fee-free ATM withdrawals up to €200/month.
- 3 commission-free stock trades per month.
- Purchase insurance, disposable virtual cards, and Junior accounts.

### 3. Premium — **£7.99/month** (or £80/year)
- Unlimited fee-free currency exchange (no weekend surcharge).
- Fee-free ATM withdrawals up to €400/month.
- 5 commission-free stock trades per month.
- Travel insurance included.
- Access to lifestyle partner subscriptions (e.g. Deliveroo, Tinder).
- Better savings rates.

### 4. Metal — **£14.99/month** (or £140/year)
- All Premium benefits, plus an exclusive stainless-steel card.
- Fee-free ATM withdrawals up to €800/month.
- 10 commission-free stock trades per month.
- Enhanced travel insurance and purchase protection, car hire excess cover.
- Broader partner subscriptions (Financial Times, ClassPass, etc.).
- Cashback on card payments.
- Subscriptions valued at up to ~£2,200/year.

### 5. Ultra — **£55/month**
- Revolut's top-end plan with benefits valued at over £4,000/year.
- Savings rate up to 4% AER (variable).
- Unlimited airport lounge access.
- 3 GB monthly global data roaming in 100+ countries.
- 10 commission-free stock trades per month; reduced commission (0.12%) on additional trades (vs 0.25% on other plans).
- Extensive partner subscriptions including FT Premium Digital, WeWork, MasterClass, Uber One, NordVPN, Headspace, Perplexity Pro, and more.
- Comprehensive insurance coverage including cancellation cover.

---

### Key Fees Across Plans

| Fee Type | Standard | Plus | Premium | Metal | Ultra |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Monthly price** | Free | £3.99 | £7.99 | £14.99 | £55 |
| **Weekend FX fee** | 1% | 0.5% | None | None | None |
| **Weekday FX fair-use limit** | £1,000/mo | £3,000/mo | Unlimited | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| **Fee-free ATM withdrawals** | €200/mo | €200/mo | €400/mo | €800/mo | Up to €2,000/mo |
| **Commission-free trades** | 1/mo | 3/mo | 5/mo | 10/mo | 10/mo |
| **Extra trade commission** | 0.25% | 0.25% | 0.25% | 0.25% | 0.12% |
| **Custody fee (investments)** | 0.12% p.a. | 0.12% p.a. | 0.12% p.a. | 0.12% p.a. | 0.12% p.a. |

Beyond ATM free limits, a 2% fee applies (minimum €1 per withdrawal).

### US-Specific Pricing
In the United States, Revolut offers three tiers (as of early 2026):
- **Standard**: $0/month
- **Premium**: $9.99/month
- **Metal**: $16.99/month

US Standard customers get up to $1,200/month in fee-free out-of-network ATM withdrawals, 10 free international remittances per month, and up to $200,000/month in commission-free crypto trading.

### Upcoming Price Changes (Europe)
Revolut has announced price increases effective **July 2026** for European markets (e.g. Portugal):
- **Premium**: rising ~10% (e.g. €10.39 → €11.43/month)
- **Metal**: rising ~12.4% (e.g. €16.63 → €18.70/month)
- **Ultra**: rising ~9% (e.g. €57.20 → €62.40/month)
- **Plus** and **Standard** remain unchanged.

Customers must decide before July 2026; silence is treated as consent to the new rates.

## Revolut Plans, Prices, and Fee Structure by Tier

Revolut offers **five personal account tiers** with escalating benefits structured as lifestyle memberships. Here's a comprehensive breakdown of each tier's pricing and how fees differ:

---

### **1. Standard — FREE**
- **Monthly price:** £0
- **Physical debit card:** £4.99
- **Currency exchange:**
  - Fee-free up to £1,000/month (weekdays only)
  - 1% fee on weekend exchanges
- **ATM withdrawals:** Fee-free up to €200/month (or 5 withdrawals, whichever comes first)
- **Stock trading:** 1 commission-free trade per month
- **Additional trade commission:** 0.25%
- **Custody fee:** 0.12% per annum
- **Basic features:** Money management, budgeting tools, international transfers

---

### **2. Plus — £3.99/month (or £40/year)**
- **Currency exchange:**
  - Fee-free up to £3,000/month
  - 0.5% weekend FX fee (reduced from Standard's 1%)
- **ATM withdrawals:** Fee-free up to €200/month
- **Stock trading:** 3 commission-free trades per month
- **Additional trade commission:** 0.25%
- **Custody fee:** 0.12% per annum
- **Additional benefits:** Purchase insurance, disposable virtual cards, Junior accounts

---

### **3. Premium — £7.99/month (or £80/year)**
- **Currency exchange:**
  - **Unlimited** fee-free currency exchange
  - **No weekend surcharge** (0% weekend FX fee)
- **ATM withdrawals:** Fee-free up to €400/month
- **Stock trading:** 5 commission-free trades per month
- **Additional trade commission:** 0.25%
- **Custody fee:** 0.12% per annum
- **Additional benefits:** Travel insurance, access to lifestyle partner subscriptions (Deliveroo, Tinder), better savings rates

---

### **4. Metal — £14.99/month (or £140/year)**
- **Currency exchange:**
  - **Unlimited** fee-free currency exchange
  - **No weekend surcharge**
- **ATM withdrawals:** Fee-free up to €800/month
- **Stock trading:** 10 commission-free trades per month
- **Additional trade commission:** 0.25%
- **Custody fee:** 0.12% per annum
- **Exclusive features:**
  - Stainless-steel card
  - Enhanced travel insurance and purchase protection
  - Car hire excess cover
  - Cashback on card payments
  - Broader partner subscriptions (Financial Times, ClassPass, etc.)
  - **Total subscription value:** ~£2,200/year

---

### **5. Ultra — £55/month**
- **Currency exchange:**
  - **Unlimited** fee-free currency exchange
  - **No weekend surcharge**
- **ATM withdrawals:** Fee-free up to €2,000/month
- **Stock trading:** 10 commission-free trades per month
- **Additional trade commission:** **0.12%** (reduced from 0.25% on other plans)
- **Custody fee:** 0.12% per annum
- **Savings rate:** Up to 4% AER (variable)
- **Premium features:**
  - Unlimited airport lounge access
  - 3 GB monthly global data roaming in 100+ countries
  - Extensive partner subscriptions: Financial Times Premium Digital, WeWork, MasterClass Full, Uber One, NordVPN Complete, Headspace, Sleep Cycle Premium, Freeletics, Picsart Gold, The Athletic, ClassPass, Perplexity Pro, Chess.com, Headway Premium, Tinder Gold, Turo
  - Comprehensive insurance including cancellation cover
  - **Total benefits valued:** Over £4,000/year

---

## **Key Fee Differences Across Tiers**

| **Fee Type** | **Standard** | **Plus** | **Premium** | **Metal** | **Ultra** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Monthly price** | Free | £3.99 | £7.99 | £14.99 | £55 |
| **Weekend FX fee** | 1% | 0.5% | None | None | None |
| **Weekday FX fair-use limit** | £1,000/mo | £3,000/mo | Unlimited | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| **Fee-free ATM withdrawals** | €200/mo | €200/mo | €400/mo | €800/mo | Up to €2,000/mo |
| **Commission-free trades** | 1/mo | 3/mo | 5/mo | 10/mo | 10/mo |
| **Extra trade commission** | 0.25% | 0.25% | 0.25% | 0.25% | 0.12% |
| **Custody fee (investments)** | 0.12% p.a. | 0.12% p.a. | 0.12% p.a. | 0.12% p.a. | 0.12% p.a. |

**Note:** Beyond ATM free limits, a 2% fee applies (minimum €1 per withdrawal).

---

## **US-Specific Pricing**

Revolut offers **three tiers** in the United States (as of early 2026):
- **Standard:** $0/month
- **Premium:** $9.99/month
- **Metal:** $16.99/month

US Standard customers receive:
- Up to $1,200/month in fee-free out-of-network ATM withdrawals
- 10 free international remittances per month
- Up to $200,000/month in commission-free crypto trading

---

## **Upcoming Price Changes (Europe — Effective July 2026)**

Revolut has announced price increases for European markets (e.g., Portugal):
- **Premium:** Rising ~10% (e.g., €10.39 → €11.43/month)
- **Metal:** Rising ~12.4% (e.g., €16.63 → €18.70/month)
- **Ultra:** Rising ~9% (e.g., €57.20 → €62.40/month)
- **Plus** (€4.15) and **Standard** remain unchanged

Customers must decide before July 2026; silence will be treated as consent to the new rates.

---

## **Summary of Key Tier Differences**

The main differentiators across tiers are:

1. **Currency exchange limits and weekend fees:** Standard and Plus have monthly limits and weekend fees, while Premium, Metal, and Ultra offer unlimited fee-free exchange with no weekend surcharges.

2. **ATM withdrawal limits:** Progressively increase from €200/month (Standard/Plus) to €2,000/month (Ultra).

3. **Stock trading allowances:** Range from 1 free trade/month (Standard) to 10 free trades/month (Metal/Ultra), with Ultra offering a lower commission rate (0.12% vs 0.25%) on additional trades.

4. **Lifestyle benefits:** Higher tiers include travel insurance, partner subscriptions, cashback, airport lounge access, and global data roaming, with total benefit values ranging from £2,200/year (Metal) to over £4,000/year (Ultra).

5. **Savings rates:** Ultra offers the highest savings rate at up to 4% AER (variable).

query: What new products and features has the competitor (Revolut) recently announced?
answer:
Revolut has recently announced a significant number of new products and features across multiple areas:

## Global Banking Expansion

**Colombia Banking Licence (September 15, 2026):** Revolut secured its sixth banking licence worldwide from Colombia's Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC). The company plans to launch deposit accounts, high-yield savings accounts, multiple credit cards, and unsecured consumer loans, with operations starting in 2027. Around 200,000 Colombians are already on the waitlist, and Revolut is investing $62 million in the country.

**Swiss Banking Licence Application (September 16, 2026):** Revolut applied to FINMA for a Swiss banking licence and committed CHF 150 million in investment over five years. If approved, it would offer Swiss deposit protection, local IBANs, salary accounts, eBill electronic bill payment, merchant acquiring, and eventually Pillar 3a retirement savings and TWINT mobile payment integration.

**U.S. National Bank Charter (September 3, 2026):** Revolut received conditional approval from the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to form a national bank, which would offer traditional banking alongside digital asset custody, cross-border crypto payments, and a company-branded stablecoin.

**Full Banking Licences Activated in 2026:** Revolut activated full banking licences in the UK (March 2026), France, Australia, and Mexico (its first bank outside Europe).

## Stablecoins

**EURR (Euro-backed Stablecoin):** Revolut began rolling out EURR to selected customers in Denmark, Poland, and Portugal in August 2026, with plans to expand across the European Economic Area.

**GBP Stablecoin:** Revolut is participating in the FCA sandbox for a GBP-denominated stablecoin.

## Institutional Crypto

**Institutional Crypto Business Build-out:** Revolut hired Nilesh Khatwani (formerly of Crypto.com) as Global Head of Institutional Sales, Crypto, to develop products for companies and professional users. Current offerings include:
- **Crypto for Business:** Allows businesses to buy, sell, and hold digital assets for corporate treasury
- **Revolut X for Business:** A spot-trading venue with lower fees, analytical tools, and Business account integration

**Dubai Virtual-Asset Services:** Revolut is preparing to offer regulated virtual-asset services in the UAE following its payments licence there.

## AI & Revolut X Enhancements

**AI Assistant Integration on Revolut X (July 2026):** Revolut connected its crypto exchange to third-party AI assistants including Claude and Gemini, allowing customers to analyze markets and place trades through natural-language prompts.

**AIR (Revolut AI):** Listed as a product category on Revolut's platform, indicating an AI-powered financial assistant feature.

## Investment Products

Revolut's platform now includes:
- Stocks
- Robo-Advisor
- ETFs
- Bonds
- Flexible Cash Funds
- Instant Access Savings

## Other Features

**Data Plans:** Mobile connectivity/data plans available through the app.

**RevPoints:** A loyalty/rewards programme integrated into the spending experience.

Revolut now serves over 80 million customers globally, posted $6 billion in revenue in 2025 (up 46% year-over-year) with $2.3 billion in pre-tax profit, and is targeting 100 million customers by mid-2027.

The company lists Swiss IBANs, salary accounts, electronic bill payment via eBill and payment processing for merchants as possible features. Later on, it also plans to add private retirement savings through Pillar 3a and to integrate TWINT, the Swiss mobile payment service. [...] Meanwhile, FINMA has yet to decide on Revolut’s Swiss expansion plans. Approval could bring Revolut closer to a full local banking offering. Which additional services customers will actually be able to use, and on what terms, will become clear once they launch.

## Revolut — Recently Announced New Products & Features (as of September 2026)

Revolut has been on an aggressive expansion and product-launch spree in recent months. Here are the key announcements:

### 🏦 Global Banking Expansion
- **Colombia banking licence** (Sep 15, 2026): Revolut secured its sixth banking licence worldwide from Colombia's Superintendencia Financiera (SFC). It plans to launch deposit accounts, high-yield savings, multiple credit cards, and unsecured consumer loans, with operations starting in 2027. Around 200,000 Colombians are already on the waitlist. Revolut is investing $62 million in the country.
- **Swiss banking licence application** (Sep 16, 2026): Revolut applied to FINMA for a Swiss banking licence and committed CHF 150 million in investment over five years. If approved, it would offer Swiss deposit protection, local IBANs, salary accounts, eBill electronic bill payment, merchant acquiring, and eventually Pillar 3a retirement savings and TWINT mobile payment integration.
- **U.S. national bank charter** (Sep 3, 2026): Revolut received conditional approval from the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to form a national bank, which would offer traditional banking alongside digital asset custody, cross-border crypto payments, and a company-branded stablecoin.
- **Full banking licences activated in 2026** in the UK (March 2026), France, Australia, and Mexico (first bank outside Europe).

### 💰 Stablecoins
- **EURR (euro-backed stablecoin)**: Revolut began rolling out EURR to selected customers in Denmark, Poland, and Portugal in August 2026, with plans to expand across the European Economic Area.
- **GBP stablecoin**: Revolut is participating in the FCA sandbox for a GBP-denominated stablecoin.

### 🪙 Institutional Crypto
- **Institutional crypto business build-out**: Revolut hired Nilesh Khatwani (formerly of Crypto.com) as Global Head of Institutional Sales, Crypto, to develop products for companies and professional users. Current offerings include **Crypto for Business** (buy, sell, hold digital assets for corporate treasury) and **Revolut X for Business** (spot-trading venue with lower fees, analytical tools, and Business account integration).
- **Dubai virtual-asset services**: Revolut is preparing to offer regulated virtual-asset services in the UAE following its payments licence there.

### 🤖 AI & Revolut X Enhancements
- **AI assistant integration on Revolut X** (July 2026): Revolut connected its crypto exchange to third-party AI assistants including Claude and Gemini, allowing customers to analyze markets and place trades through natural-language prompts.
- **AIR (Revolut AI)**: Listed as a product category on Revolut's platform, indicating an AI-powered financial assistant feature.

### 📊 Investment Products
- Revolut's platform now includes **Stocks, Robo-Advisor, ETFs, and Bonds** as investment verticals, along with **Flexible Cash Funds** and **Instant Access Savings**.

### 📱 Other Features
- **Data Plans**: Mobile connectivity/data plans available through the app.
- **RevPoints**: A loyalty/rewards programme integrated into the spending experience.

**Data Plans:** Mobile connectivity/data plans available through the app.

**RevPoints:** A loyalty/rewards programme integrated into the spending experience.

query: What do users value and complain about in the competitor's (Revolut) app reviews?
answer:
## Revolut App Reviews: What Users Value and Complain About

Based on analysis of Revolut app reviews, here's what users value and complain about:

### Overall Ratings
As of September 2026, Revolut holds a **4.8–4.9 out of 5** rating across app stores, with over **200,000–329,000 reviews** depending on the region. Overall user sentiment is positive, though recurring pain points persist.

---

### What Users Value Most

1. **Speed and ease of use** — Users consistently praise the app for being intuitive, simple, and feature-rich. Long-term users describe it as their primary banking app, even over traditional bank accounts.

2. **International capabilities** — Multi-currency support, interbank exchange rates, and seamless use abroad are among the most-cited benefits. Travelling and sending money internationally are top use cases.

3. **All-in-one financial management** — Users appreciate managing daily finances, transfers, crypto, and investments in a single app.

4. **Security features** — Single-use virtual cards for online shopping, two-factor authentication, and 24/7 fraud monitoring are highlighted as valued protections.

5. **Continuous improvement** — Multiple reviewers note that Revolut keeps adding features and improving quality over time.

**User quotes:**
- *"It's simple, full of features, and easy to use."* — Michael, UK
- *"The app makes my financial life much simpler and more secure."* — Carolina, Italy
- *"Revolut is amazing. It's my main account for travelling or sending money abroad. Service is fast, customer support is helpful, and Revolut keeps improving in quality."* — Pawel, Japan
- *"I've been using Revolut for the past 5 years and it's my main account, even though I have 4+ accounts."* — Michael, UK

---

### Common Complaints and Pain Points

1. **Customer support quality** — This is the most persistent complaint. Users report slow responses, over-reliance on AI chatbots and scripted answers, and difficulty reaching a human agent — especially when locked out of their account.

2. **Account restrictions and frozen funds** — Users report accounts being frozen or restricted without clear explanation, with funds inaccessible while compliance checks run. Resolution can be slow.

3. **Hidden fees** — Complaints about unexpected charges, particularly around crypto transactions and subscription cancellations.

4. **Fraud and scam complaints** — Revolut has led UK fraud complaint tables for three consecutive years. In 2025, customers brought **3,208 fraud complaints** to the Financial Ombudsman Service (1,875 authorised push payment fraud and 1,333 unauthorised fraud). The FOS uphold rate for Revolut APP fraud cases was **37%**.

5. **Data privacy concerns** — Users have raised concerns about Revolut sharing data with third-party apps. Most recently (September 2026), a security incident involved attackers using a fake government email to obtain sensitive customer data — including ID documents, verification selfies, account details, and transaction histories.

6. **Difficulty deleting accounts** — Some users report challenges when trying to close their accounts or access support after being locked out.

---

### Summary

Revolut is widely valued for its speed, international money features, and all-in-one convenience, earning very high app store ratings. However, customer support responsiveness, account freezing practices, fraud handling, and recent data security incidents remain significant areas of user concern.

## Revolut App Reviews: User Complaints, Feedback & What Users Value

### Overall Ratings
As of September 2026, Revolut holds a **4.8–4.9 out of 5** rating across app stores, with over **200,000–329,000 reviews** depending on the region. Overall user sentiment is positive, though recurring pain points persist.

---

### What Users Value Most

- **Speed and ease of use** — Users consistently praise the app for being intuitive, simple, and feature-rich. Long-term users describe it as their primary banking app, even over traditional bank accounts.
- **International capabilities** — Multi-currency support, interbank exchange rates, and seamless use abroad are among the most-cited benefits. Travelling and sending money internationally are top use cases.
- **All-in-one financial management** — Users appreciate managing daily finances, transfers, crypto, and investments in a single app.
- **Security features** — Single-use virtual cards for online shopping, two-factor authentication, and 24/7 fraud monitoring are highlighted as valued protections.
- **Continuous improvement** — Multiple reviewers note that Revolut keeps adding features and improving quality over time.

> *"It's simple, full of features, and easy to use."* — Michael, UK
> *"The app makes my financial life much simpler and more secure."* — Carolina, Italy

---

### Common Complaints and Pain Points

1. **Customer support quality** — This is the most persistent complaint. Users report slow responses, over-reliance on AI chatbots and scripted answers, and difficulty reaching a human agent — especially when locked out of their account.

2. **Account restrictions and frozen funds** — Users report accounts being frozen or restricted without clear explanation, with funds inaccessible while compliance checks run. Resolution can be slow.

3. **Hidden fees** — Complaints about unexpected charges, particularly around crypto transactions and subscription cancellations.

4. **Fraud and scam complaints** — Revolut has led UK fraud complaint tables for three consecutive years. In 2025, customers brought **3,208 fraud complaints** to the Financial Ombudsman Service (1,875 authorised push payment fraud and 1,333 unauthorised fraud). The FOS uphold rate for Revolut APP fraud cases was **37%**.

5. **Data privacy concerns** — Users have raised concerns about Revolut sharing data with third-party apps. Most recently (September 2026), a security incident involved attackers using a fake government email to obtain sensitive customer data — including ID documents, verification selfies, account details, and transaction histories.

6. **Difficulty deleting accounts** — Some users report challenges when trying to close their accounts or access support after being locked out.

---

### Summary

Revolut is widely valued for its speed, international money features, and all-in-one convenience, earning very high app store ratings. However, customer support responsiveness, account freezing practices, fraud handling, and recent data security incidents remain significant areas of user concern.

answer:
BBVA publishes comprehensive senior-position profiles and requirements for leadership roles, covering governance standards, selection criteria, diversity commitments, and core competencies:

## Fit-and-Proper and Suitability Standards

Directors and senior executives must meet "fit & proper" criteria established in BBVA's governance policies. They must demonstrate:
- Recognised commercial and professional reputation
- Adequate knowledge and experience to carry out their duties
- Ability to exercise good governance of the Company

The Board of Directors assesses suitability requirements following a report from the Appointments and Corporate Governance Committee.

## Board Composition Requirements

BBVA maintains strict board composition rules:
- At least 50% of the Board of Directors must be independent members
- The Board targets a minimum of 40% female representation, which it currently meets
- Non-executive directors must represent an ample majority over executive directors (currently 13 out of 15 directors, or 87%, are non-executive)
- 10 directors have "independent" status, representing 67% of Board members
- The Board currently has six female directors, meeting the 40% target

## Gender Equality as Strategic Priority

Gender equality is a strategic priority for BBVA across the entire business:
- The bank applies the **Rooney rule**, requiring that at least half of the final candidates for internal senior-position appointments be women
- BBVA has achieved close to 47% female representation in leadership positions
- In 2021, 52% of promotions went to women
- Overall workforce representation is 53% female against 47% male

## Selection Criteria for Directors

Candidates for director positions must meet the following criteria:
- **Legal eligibility** under applicable law
- **Relevant academic training and professional experience** in areas such as:
  - Banking
  - Finance
  - Risk management
  - Regulatory affairs
  - Strategic planning
- **Leadership capability**
- **Financial and business literacy**
- **Board service experience**
- **Corporate governance expertise**
- **Risk management knowledge**
- Ability to contribute to corporate governance

## Typical Senior-Executive Roles

BBVA's senior leadership structure includes positions such as:
- Global Head of Engineering
- Global Head of Data
- Global Head of Digital Banks
- Head of Legal Services
- Global Head of Finance
- Head of Global Risk Management
- Global Head of Sustainability and Corporate & Investment Banking (CIB)
- Global Head of Retail Client Solutions
- Global Head of Talent & Culture
- Head of Risk for South America and Türkiye
- Country Manager for Mexico
- Country Manager for Türkiye
- Other C-level functions

These roles are typically filled by individuals with extensive internal experience and sector expertise.

## Core Competencies for Senior Leaders

Required skills and competencies include:
- Strong communication and influence abilities across all organizational levels, including top leadership
- Ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment
- Capability to drive cross-functional projects
- Strong analytical skills
- Presentation and business literacy abilities

## Employment Eligibility (U.S. Roles)

For senior-associate positions in BBVA's U.S. Corporate & Investment Banking unit:
- Candidates must be eligible to work in the United States
- The bank does not sponsor visas for these positions

## Governance and Selection Process

BBVA's director renewal and selection processes are governed by principles ensuring:
- **Legal compliance** with requirements necessary to perform the role
- **Adequate board composition** at all times
- **Transparent and equitable** director-renewal and selection processes
- **Sound decision-making** by BBVA's corporate bodies
- Assessment of potential board-committee members based on **knowledge, skills, and experience**
- **Promotion of diversity and inclusion** in all selection processes
- Selection procedures free from implicit bias that could lead to discrimination
- Encouragement of diversity based on gender, academic profile, professional experience, knowledge, disability, origin, or age

The selection and renewal processes are directed toward promoting BBVA's Purpose, business strategy, objectives, values, and long-term interests of the BBVA Group.

{"content":"**BBVA senior‑leadership profiles and requirements**

- **Fit‑and‑proper and suitability standards** – Directors and senior executives must have recognised commercial and professional reputation, adequate knowledge and experience, and be able to exercise good governance. They must satisfy the “fit & proper” criteria set out in BBVA’s governance policies. (see 03d2cfb5‑01c3‑4117‑8d5e‑35496796fe40, 9ce54839‑a253‑487b‑a924‑f9287e02e82f)

- **Board composition rules** – At least 50 % of the Board of Directors must be independent members, and the Board targets a minimum of 40 % female representation, which it currently meets. (see a226a61f‑fbbd‑4810‑9d72‑08c35e220571, 4e2e6054‑0ce2‑47a3‑9d34‑9e600b595208)

- **Gender‑equality priority** – Gender equality is a strategic priority for BBVA. The bank applies the Rooney rule, requiring that at least half of the final candidates for internal senior‑position appointments be women, and it has achieved close to 47 % female representation in leadership roles. (see d7460f61‑9140‑4bd9‑8363‑825ec2a57360, 50d3facf‑2e27‑4a1f‑939e‑1bb4b672d053)

- **Selection criteria for directors** – Candidates must be eligible under applicable law, possess relevant academic training and professional experience (e.g., banking, finance, risk, regulatory affairs, strategic planning), demonstrate leadership, financial/business literacy, and the ability to contribute to corporate governance. (see a38bb27d‑2fd7‑4923‑8bae‑077dae80c68c)

- **Typical senior‑executive roles** – BBVA’s senior leadership includes positions such as Global Head of Engineering, Global Head of Data, Global Head of Digital Banks, Head of Legal Services, Head of Risk for South America and Turkey, Country Manager for Mexico, and other C‑level functions. These roles are usually filled by individuals with extensive internal experience and sector expertise. (see ac248819‑9e8c‑41a9‑80dc‑d8d610df2443, cd40fa33‑ab9a‑48ff‑80bc‑af8a19e55251)

- **Employment eligibility for U.S. roles** – Senior‑associate positions in BBVA’s U.S. Corporate & Investment Banking unit require candidates to be eligible to work in the United States; the bank does not sponsor visas for these roles. (see 3633671a‑a943‑417d‑a051‑212a73a1a94d)

- **Core competencies for senior leaders** – Required skills include the ability to communicate and influence at all organisational levels, manage competing priorities, drive cross‑functional projects, and possess strong analytical and presentation abilities. (see b66fab01‑427d‑496e‑b9f5‑543c40441b8e)

- **Governance and selection process** – BBVA’s directors must comply with legal requirements, ensure adequate board composition, identify suitable candidates, and maintain transparency and equity in the director‑renewal and selection processes. The bank assesses the profile of potential board‑committee members based on knowledge, skills, and experience, while promoting diversity and inclusion. (see 7fb584b8‑1b08‑434e‑b773‑3615a5296dfc, c099be91‑1293‑4177‑ba6c‑59bf125ec05e, e80fc907‑d98b‑4702‑893d‑3404e96dc151)

structuredContent.content:
**BBVA senior‑leadership profiles and requirements**

- **Fit‑and‑proper and suitability standards** – Directors and senior executives must have recognised commercial and professional reputation, adequate knowledge and experience, and be able to exercise good governance. They must satisfy the “fit & proper” criteria set out in BBVA’s governance policies. (see 03d2cfb5‑01c3‑4117‑8d5e‑35496796fe40, 9ce54839‑a253‑487b‑a924‑f9287e02e82f)

- **Board composition rules** – At least 50 % of the Board of Directors must be independent members, and the Board targets a minimum of 40 % female representation, which it currently meets. (see a226a61f‑fbbd‑4810‑9d72‑08c35e220571, 4e2e6054‑0ce2‑47a3‑9d34‑9e600b595208)

- **Gender‑equality priority** – Gender equality is a strategic priority for BBVA. The bank applies the Rooney rule, requiring that at least half of the final candidates for internal senior‑position appointments be women, and it has achieved close to 47 % female representation in leadership roles. (see d7460f61‑9140‑4bd9‑8363‑825ec2a57360, 50d3facf‑2e27‑4a1f‑939e‑1bb4b672d053)

- **Selection criteria for directors** – Candidates must be eligible under applicable law, possess relevant academic training and professional experience (e.g., banking, finance, risk, regulatory affairs, strategic planning), demonstrate leadership, financial/business literacy, and the ability to contribute to corporate governance. (see a38bb27d‑2fd7‑4923‑8bae‑077dae80c68c)

- **Typical senior‑executive roles** – BBVA’s senior leadership includes positions such as Global Head of Engineering, Global Head of Data, Global Head of Digital Banks, Head of Legal Services, Head of Risk for South America and Turkey, Country Manager for Mexico, and other C‑level functions. These roles are usually filled by individuals with extensive internal experience and sector expertise. (see ac248819‑9e8c‑41a9‑80dc‑d8d610df2443, cd40fa33‑ab9a‑48ff‑80bc‑af8a19e55251)

- **Employment eligibility for U.S. roles** – Senior‑associate positions in BBVA’s U.S. Corporate & Investment Banking unit require candidates to be eligible to work in the United States; the bank does not sponsor visas for these roles. (see 3633671a‑a943‑417d‑a051‑212a73a1a94d)

- **Core competencies for senior leaders** – Required skills include the ability to communicate and influence at all organisational levels, manage competing priorities, drive cross‑functional projects, and possess strong analytical and presentation abilities. (see b66fab01‑427d‑496e‑b9f5‑543c40441b8e)

- **Governance and selection process** – BBVA’s directors must comply with legal requirements, ensure adequate board composition, identify suitable candidates, and maintain transparency and equity in the director‑renewal and selection processes. The bank assesses the profile of potential board‑committee members based on knowledge, skills, and experience, while promoting diversity and inclusion. (see 7fb584b8‑1b08‑434e‑b773‑3615a5296dfc, c099be91‑1293‑4177‑ba6c‑59bf125ec05e, e80fc907‑d98b‑4702‑893d‑3404e96dc151)

In summary, BBVA’s senior‑leadership recruitment combines strict fit‑and‑proper standards, a focus on independent and gender‑balanced board composition, and a demand for deep sector expertise, leadership capability, and cross‑functional skills.

explainability.content: Directors and senior executives must meet fit‑and‑proper and suitability standards, demonstrating recognised commercial reputation, adequate knowledge and experience, and the ability to exercise good governance.
BBVA’s board must have at least 50 % independent members and aims for a minimum of 40 % female representation, which it currently achieves.

Gender equality is a strategic priority; BBVA applies the Rooney rule, requiring at least half of final internal senior‑position candidates to be women, resulting in about 47 % female leadership representation.

Selection criteria for directors include legal eligibility, relevant academic and professional background (banking, finance, risk, regulatory affairs, strategic planning), leadership, financial literacy, and governance experience.

Typical senior‑executive roles at BBVA include Global Heads of Engineering, Data, Digital Banks, Legal Services, Risk, Country Managers, and other C‑level functions, filled by individuals with extensive internal experience and sector expertise.
U.S. senior‑associate positions in BBVA’s Corporate & Investment Banking unit require candidates to be eligible to work in the United States; the bank does not sponsor visas.

Core competencies for senior leaders include strong communication and influence across all organisational levels, ability to manage competing priorities, drive cross‑functional projects, and possess analytical and presentation skills.

The governance and selection process mandates legal compliance, adequate board composition, transparent and equitable director‑renewal procedures, and assessment of candidates’ knowledge, skills, and experience while promoting diversity and inclusion.

BBVA publishes comprehensive senior-position profiles and requirements for leadership roles, covering governance standards, selection criteria, diversity commitments, and core competencies:

## Fit-and-Proper and Suitability Standards

Directors and senior executives must meet "fit & proper" criteria established in BBVA's governance policies. They must demonstrate:
- Recognised commercial and professional reputation
- Adequate knowledge and experience to carry out their duties
- Ability to exercise good governance of the Company

The Board of Directors assesses suitability requirements following a report from the Appointments and Corporate Governance Committee.

## Board Composition Requirements

BBVA maintains strict board composition rules:
- At least 50% of the Board of Directors must be independent members
- The Board targets a minimum of 40% female representation, which it currently meets
- Non-executive directors must represent an ample majority over executive directors (currently 13 out of 15 directors, or 87%, are non-executive)
- 10 directors have "independent" status, representing 67% of Board members
- The Board currently has six female directors, meeting the 40% target

## Gender Equality as Strategic Priority

Gender equality is a strategic priority for BBVA across the entire business:
- The bank applies the **Rooney rule**, requiring that at least half of the final candidates for internal senior-position appointments be women
- BBVA has achieved close to 47% female representation in leadership positions
- In 2021, 52% of promotions went to women
- Overall workforce representation is 53% female against 47% male

## Selection Criteria for Directors

Candidates for director positions must meet the following criteria:
- **Legal eligibility** under applicable law
- **Relevant academic training and professional experience** in areas such as:
  - Banking
  - Finance
  - Risk management
  - Regulatory affairs
  - Strategic planning
- **Leadership capability**
- **Financial and business literacy**
- **Board service experience**
- **Corporate governance expertise**
- **Risk management knowledge**
- Ability to contribute to corporate governance

## Typical Senior-Executive Roles

BBVA's senior leadership structure includes positions such as:
- Global Head of Engineering
- Global Head of Data
- Global Head of Digital Banks
- Head of Legal Services
- Global Head of Finance
- Head of Global Risk Management
- Global Head of Sustainability and Corporate & Investment Banking (CIB)
- Global Head of Retail Client Solutions
- Global Head of Talent & Culture
- Head of Risk for South America and Türkiye
- Country Manager for Mexico
- Country Manager for Türkiye
- Other C-level functions

These roles are typically filled by individuals with extensive internal experience and sector expertise.

## Core Competencies for Senior Leaders

Required skills and competencies include:
- Strong communication and influence abilities across all organizational levels, including top leadership
- Ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment
- Capability to drive cross-functional projects
- Strong analytical skills
- Presentation and business literacy abilities

## Employment Eligibility (U.S. Roles)

For senior-associate positions in BBVA's U.S. Corporate & Investment Banking unit:
- Candidates must be eligible to work in the United States
- The bank does not sponsor visas for these positions

## Governance and Selection Process

BBVA's director renewal and selection processes are governed by principles ensuring:
- **Legal compliance** with requirements necessary to perform the role
- **Adequate board composition** at all times
- **Transparent and equitable** director-renewal and selection processes
- **Sound decision-making** by BBVA's corporate bodies
- Assessment of potential board-committee members based on **knowledge, skills, and experience**
- **Promotion of diversity and inclusion** in all selection processes
- Selection procedures free from implicit bias that could lead to discrimination
- Encouragement of diversity based on gender, academic profile, professional experience, knowledge, disability, origin, or age

The selection and renewal processes are directed toward promoting BBVA's Purpose, business strategy, objectives, values, and long-term interests of the BBVA Group.

answer:
## BNP Paribas Leadership Organizational Structure and Responsibilities

BNP Paribas has a comprehensive leadership structure consisting of **General Management** (6 members) and an **Executive Committee** that brings together the General Management plus 14 other members who head the Group's major business lines and central functions. The committee meets **at least once a week** and is responsible for setting and implementing BNP Paribas' strategy.

---

### **GENERAL MANAGEMENT (6 Members)**

The General Management comprises a Chief Executive Officer (CEO), two Chief Operating Officers (COOs), and three Deputy Chief Operating Officers (Deputy COOs):

#### **1. Jean-Laurent Bonnafé — Director and Chief Executive Officer**
- **Responsibilities:** Bears responsibility for the management of the entire Group and is invested with extensive powers. All operational activities and Group functions fall under his direct responsibility. He leads the strategic direction of BNP Paribas and oversees all business divisions and central functions.

#### **2. Yann Gérardin — Chief Operating Officer**
- **Responsibilities:** Executive Chairman of Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB). He oversees one of the Group's three core business divisions, which serves corporate and institutional clients with banking, markets, and securities services.

#### **3. Thierry Laborde — Chief Operating Officer**
- **Responsibilities:** In charge of Commercial, Personal Banking & Services (CPBS). He oversees the division that serves individual customers, community associations, entrepreneurs, and SMEs across BNP Paribas' domestic markets and international operations.

#### **4. Renaud Dumora — Deputy Chief Operating Officer**
- **Responsibilities:** In charge of Investment & Protection Services (IPS). He oversees the division that includes asset management (BNP Paribas Asset Management) and insurance services (BNP Paribas Cardif). He also serves as Chairman of BNP Paribas Cardif. Sandro Pierri (CEO of BNP Paribas Asset Management) reports to him.

#### **5. Yannick Jung — Deputy Chief Operating Officer**
- **Responsibilities:** In charge of Commercial & Personal Banking in the Eurozone within CPBS. He focuses on the retail and commercial banking operations specifically in the Eurozone markets.

#### **6. Olivier Osty — Deputy Chief Operating Officer**
- **Responsibilities:** Chief Executive Officer of Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB), effective 1 September 2025. He manages the day-to-day operations of the CIB division, working alongside Yann Gérardin who serves as Executive Chairman.

---

### **OTHER EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE MEMBERS — Heads of Businesses & Central Functions**

#### **Business Line Heads:**

**7. Pauline Leclerc-Glorieux**
- **Role:** Director and Chief Executive Officer of BNP Paribas Cardif (Insurance)
- **Responsibilities:** Leads the Group's insurance business, which is part of the Investment & Protection Services division. She succeeded Renaud Dumora in this role in May 2021.

**8. Sandro Pierri**
- **Role:** Chief Executive Officer of BNP Paribas Asset Management
- **Responsibilities:** Leads the newly unified BNP Paribas Asset Management platform, which is strategically positioned within the Group's integrated model. He joined the Executive Committee on 30 March 2026 and reports to Renaud Dumora. He brings asset management expertise to support the Group's growth trajectory.

**9. Gilles Zeitoun**
- **Role:** Director and Chief Executive Officer of BNP Paribas Personal Finance
- **Responsibilities:** Leads the consumer credit business in Europe. He joined the Executive Committee effective 1 January 2026, succeeding Charlotte Dennery. He leverages his broad international experience to reinforce the leadership of BNP Paribas' consumer credit operations.

**10. Isabelle Loc**
- **Role:** Head of Commercial & Personal Banking in France
- **Responsibilities:** Oversees the retail and commercial banking operations in France, one of BNP Paribas' four domestic markets in Europe. She reports to Thierry Laborde and is responsible for steering the transformation of commercial banking in France.

#### **Central Function Heads:**

**11. Lars Machenil — Chief Financial Officer (CFO)**
- **Responsibilities:** Oversees the full scope of the Group's financial management, including:
  - Financial reporting and performance management
  - Strategic financial planning and mid-term targets
  - Capital management and regulatory discussions (e.g., with the ECB)
  - M&A and deal structuring
  - Risk and liquidity oversight
  - Investor and market communications
- He became Group CFO in 2012 and is a key spokesperson for BNP Paribas on financial matters, regularly appearing on Bloomberg TV, CNBC, and in analyst calls. He also serves on the boards of BNP Paribas Bank Polska and BNP Paribas Personal Finance SA.

**12. Frank Roncey — Chief Risk Officer (CRO)**
- **Responsibilities:** Oversees risk management across the Group, ensuring appropriate risk controls and frameworks are in place to protect the bank's stability and performance.

**13. Stéphanie Maarek — Chief Compliance Officer (Head of Compliance)**
- **Responsibilities:** Leads the Group's integrated compliance function across all BNP Paribas businesses and geographies. Her responsibilities include:
  - Managing non-compliance risks, including conduct risk, operational risk, and regulatory risk
  - Continuing the transformation of the compliance function to reinforce expertise across all domains
  - Contributing to the Group's strategic plan (GTS 2025)
  - Reporting directly to the General Management
- She was appointed Chief Compliance Officer on 1 January 2023, succeeding Nathalie Hartmann. She previously served as Chief Conduct and Control Officer for Global Markets and CIB since December 2017.

**14. Philippe Maillard — Group Chief Operating Officer**
- **Responsibilities:** Oversees the Technology & Operational Performance perimeter, effective 11 February 2025. His responsibilities include:
  - IT Group (Group Information Technology)
  - Group Data Office
  - Facilities management
  - Procurement
  - Internal consulting
- He reports to Jean-Laurent Bonnafé and is responsible for improving operational performance, developing technological resources, and strengthening cross-functional collaboration across the Group's business lines. The Group Chief Information Officer and Group Head of Human Resources report to him. He replaced Laurent David in this position and joined the Executive Committee from his previous role as COO of the Corporate & Institutional Banking division.

**15. Sofia Merlo — Head of Human Resources**
- **Responsibilities:** Oversees human resources strategy, talent management, and organizational development across the Group. She is set to retire on 1 July 2026 and will be succeeded by Sarah Roussel.

**16. Sarah Roussel — Head of Human Resources (effective 1 July 2026)**
- **Responsibilities:** Will succeed Sofia Merlo as Group Head of Human Resources. She will report to Philippe Maillard and be responsible for continuing the development and transformation policies that support BNP Paribas' business lines, countries, and functions. She was previously Chief Executive Officer of Arval France.

**17. Elise Hermant — Head of Communications**
- **Responsibilities:** Manages the Group's reputation and image management, overseeing all communications functions. She joined the Executive Committee to bring communications strategy to the highest governance level.

**18. Anne Pointet — Head of Company Engagement**
- **Responsibilities:** Ensures the Group's positioning in actions on behalf of the environment and social inclusion, supporting the industrialization of sustainability issues as customers increasingly expect a just transition. She oversees Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and works with Laurence Pessez (Deputy Head of Company Engagement in charge of CSR) and Isabelle Giordano (Head of Group Philanthropy and General Delegate of the BNP Paribas Foundation).

**19. Marc Camus — Group Chief Information Officer**
- **Responsibilities:** Leads the IT department and drives the Group's digital strategy and innovation to meet client needs. He succeeded Bernard Gavgani on 1 April 2025 and reports to Philippe Maillard.

---

### **KEY STRUCTURAL FEATURES**

**Three Core Business Divisions:**
1. **Commercial, Personal Banking & Services (CPBS)** — overseen by COO Thierry Laborde
2. **Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB)** — led by COO Yann Gérardin (Executive Chairman) and Deputy COO Olivier Osty (CEO)
3. **Investment & Protection Services (IPS)** — overseen by Deputy COO Renaud Dumora

**Central Functions Represented:**
- Risk (Frank Roncey)
- Finance (Lars Machenil)
- Compliance (Stéphanie Maarek)
- Human Resources (Sofia Merlo / Sarah Roussel)
- Technology & Operations (Philippe Maillard)
- Communications (Elise Hermant)
- Company Engagement (Anne Pointet)

**Recent Leadership Appointments (2025-2026):**
- **Sandro Pierri** joined the Executive Committee on 30 March 2026 as CEO of BNP Paribas Asset Management
- **Gilles Zeitoun** joined the Executive Committee on 1 January 2026 as CEO of BNP Paribas Personal Finance
- **Philippe Maillard** was appointed Group Chief Operating Officer on 11 February 2025
- **Marc Camus** was appointed Group Chief Information Officer on 1 April 2025
- **Sarah Roussel** will become Group Head of Human Resources on 1 July 2026

This leadership structure reflects BNP Paribas' integrated model, combining strong business line leadership with robust central functions to support the Group's strategy, performance, and stability while contributing to a sustainable future.

{"content":"## BNP Paribas Executive Committee — Leadership Structure & Responsibilities

### Overview

The Executive Committee of BNP Paribas brings together the **General Management** (6 members) plus **14 other members** who head the Group's major business lines and central functions. The committee meets **at least once a week** and is responsible for setting and implementing BNP Paribas' strategy.

---

### General Management (6 members)

The General Management comprises a **Chief Executive Officer (CEO)**, two **Chief Operating Officers (COOs)**, and three **Deputy Chief Operating Officers (Deputy COOs)**:

| Name | Role |
|---|---|
| **Jean-Laurent Bonnafé** | Director and Chief Executive Officer — bears responsibility for the management of the Group; all operational activities and Group functions fall under his direct responsibility |
| **Yann Gérardin** | Chief Operating Officer; Executive Chairman of Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB) |
| **Thierry Laborde** | Chief Operating Officer, in charge of Commercial, Personal Banking & Services (CPBS) |
| **Renaud Dumora** | Deputy Chief Operating Officer, in charge of Investment & Protection Services (IPS) |
| **Yannick Jung** | Deputy Chief Operating Officer, in charge of Commercial & Personal Banking in the Eurozone within CPBS |
| **Olivier Osty** | Deputy Chief Operating Officer and Chief Executive Officer of Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB) (effective 1 September 2025) |

---

### Other Executive Committee Members — Heads of Businesses & Central Functions

| Name | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| **Elise Hermant** | Head of Communications |
| **Pauline Leclerc-Glorieux** | CEO of BNP Paribas Cardif (Insurance) |
| **Isabelle Loc** | Head of Commercial & Personal Banking in France |
| **Stéphanie Maarek** | Executive Committee member |
| **Lars Machenil** | Executive Committee member (Finance) |
| **Philippe Maillard** | Executive Committee member |
| **Sandro Pierri** | CEO of BNP Paribas Asset Management (joined the Executive Committee on 30 March 2026) |
| **Anne Pointet** | Head of Company Engagement |
| **Frank Roncey** | Chief Risk Officer |
| **Sarah Roussel** | Head of Human Resources |
| **Sofia Merlo** | Head of Human Resources |
| **Gilles Zeitoun** | Director and CEO of BNP Paribas Personal Finance (joined the Executive Committee effective 1 January 2026) |

---

### Key Structural Features

- **Three core business divisions** are represented at the Executive Committee level:
  - **Commercial, Personal Banking & Services (CPBS)** — overseen by COO Thierry Laborde
  - **Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB)** — led by COO Yann Gérardin (Executive Chairman) and Deputy COO Olivier Osty (CEO)
  - **Investment & Protection Services (IPS)** — overseen by Deputy COO Renaud Dumora

- **Central functions** represented include Risk (Frank Roncey), Human Resources (Sofia Merlo / Sarah Roussel), Communications (Elise Hermant), and Company Engagement (Anne Pointet).

### Recent Appointments (2026)

- **Sandro Pierri** joined the Executive Committee on 30 March 2026 as CEO of BNP Paribas Asset Management, confirming the strategic positioning of the newly unified BNPP AM within the Group's integrated model.
- **Gilles Zeitoun** was appointed Director and CEO of BNP Paribas Personal Finance and joined the Executive Committee effective 1 January 2026, succeeding Charlotte Dennery.

## BNP Paribas Executive Committee — Leadership Structure & Responsibilities

### Overview

The Executive Committee of BNP Paribas brings together the **General Management** (6 members) plus **14 other members** who head the Group's major business lines and central functions. The committee meets **at least once a week** and is responsible for setting and implementing BNP Paribas' strategy.

---

### General Management (6 members)

The General Management comprises a **Chief Executive Officer (CEO)**, two **Chief Operating Officers (COOs)**, and three **Deputy Chief Operating Officers (Deputy COOs)**:

| Name | Role |
|---|---|
| **Jean-Laurent Bonnafé** | Director and Chief Executive Officer — bears responsibility for the management of the Group; all operational activities and Group functions fall under his direct responsibility |
| **Yann Gérardin** | Chief Operating Officer; Executive Chairman of Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB) |
| **Thierry Laborde** | Chief Operating Officer, in charge of Commercial, Personal Banking & Services (CPBS) |
| **Renaud Dumora** | Deputy Chief Operating Officer, in charge of Investment & Protection Services (IPS) |
| **Yannick Jung** | Deputy Chief Operating Officer, in charge of Commercial & Personal Banking in the Eurozone within CPBS |
| **Olivier Osty** | Deputy Chief Operating Officer and Chief Executive Officer of Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB) (effective 1 September 2025) |

---

### Other Executive Committee Members — Heads of Businesses & Central Functions

| Name | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| **Elise Hermant** | Head of Communications |
| **Pauline Leclerc-Glorieux** | CEO of BNP Paribas Cardif (Insurance) |
| **Isabelle Loc** | Head of Commercial & Personal Banking in France |
| **Stéphanie Maarek** | Executive Committee member |
| **Lars Machenil** | Executive Committee member (Finance) |
| **Philippe Maillard** | Executive Committee member |
| **Sandro Pierri** | CEO of BNP Paribas Asset Management (joined the Executive Committee on 30 March 2026) |
| **Anne Pointet** | Head of Company Engagement |
| **Frank Roncey** | Chief Risk Officer |
| **Sarah Roussel** | Head of Human Resources |
| **Sofia Merlo** | Head of Human Resources |
| **Gilles Zeitoun** | Director and CEO of BNP Paribas Personal Finance (joined the Executive Committee effective 1 January 2026) |

---

### Key Structural Features

- **Three core business divisions** are represented at the Executive Committee level:
  - **Commercial, Personal Banking & Services (CPBS)** — overseen by COO Thierry Laborde
  - **Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB)** — led by COO Yann Gérardin (Executive Chairman) and Deputy COO Olivier Osty (CEO)
  - **Investment & Protection Services (IPS)** — overseen by Deputy COO Renaud Dumora

- **Central functions** represented include Risk (Frank Roncey), Human Resources (Sofia Merlo / Sarah Roussel), Communications (Elise Hermant), and Company Engagement (Anne Pointet).

### Recent Appointments (2026)

- **Sandro Pierri** joined the Executive Committee on 30 March 2026 as CEO of BNP Paribas Asset Management, confirming the strategic positioning of the newly unified BNPP AM within the Group's integrated model.
- **Gilles Zeitoun** was appointed Director and CEO of BNP Paribas Personal Finance and joined the Executive Committee effective 1 January 2026, succeeding Charlotte Dennery.

{"content":"## Stéphanie Maarek — Chief Compliance Officer, BNP Paribas

### Background

Stéphanie Maarek is a graduate of **École Polytechnique** and holds a Master's in Mathematics in Finance from **New York University**. She joined BNP Paribas in **2006** within the Global Markets division and built a diversified career in **trading and risk management** across New York, London, and Paris.

### Path to Chief Compliance Officer

In **December 2017**, she was appointed **Chief Conduct and Control Officer for Global Markets and Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB)**, where she was a member of the Executive Committees of both Global Markets and CIB. In that role she was responsible for the management of **non-financial risks**: conduct, operational, and regulatory risks.

On **1 January 2023**, Stéphanie Maarek was appointed **Chief Compliance Officer (Head of Compliance) of BNP Paribas** and became a **member of the Group's Executive Committee**, succeeding Nathalie Hartmann.

### Responsibilities as Chief Compliance Officer

As Head of Compliance and Executive Committee member, Stéphanie Maarek's responsibilities encompass:

- **Leading the Group's integrated compliance function** across all BNP Paribas businesses and geographies.
- **Managing non-compliance risks**, including conduct risk, operational risk, and regulatory risk across the Group.
- **Continuing the transformation of the compliance function**, building on the work of her predecessor to reinforce expertise across all domains of non-compliance risk.
- **Contributing to the Group's strategic plan** — CEO Jean-Laurent Bonnafé expressed confidence in her ability to "continue the compliance function's transformation and thus contribute, alongside the businesses of the Group, to the success of our GTS 2025 plan."
- **Reporting to the General Management** — the compliance function sits directly under the CEO and General Management structure of BNP Paribas.

### Position in Governance

## Stéphanie Maarek — Chief Compliance Officer, BNP Paribas

### Background

Stéphanie Maarek is a graduate of **École Polytechnique** and holds a Master's in Mathematics in Finance from **New York University**. She joined BNP Paribas in **2006** within the Global Markets division and built a diversified career in **trading and risk management** across New York, London, and Paris.

### Path to Chief Compliance Officer

In **December 2017**, she was appointed **Chief Conduct and Control Officer for Global Markets and Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB)**, where she was a member of the Executive Committees of both Global Markets and CIB. In that role she was responsible for the management of **non-financial risks**: conduct, operational, and regulatory risks.

On **1 January 2023**, Stéphanie Maarek was appointed **Chief Compliance Officer (Head of Compliance) of BNP Paribas** and became a **member of the Group's Executive Committee**, succeeding Nathalie Hartmann.

### Responsibilities as Chief Compliance Officer

As Head of Compliance and Executive Committee member, Stéphanie Maarek's responsibilities encompass:

- **Leading the Group's integrated compliance function** across all BNP Paribas businesses and geographies.
- **Managing non-compliance risks**, including conduct risk, operational risk, and regulatory risk across the Group.
- **Continuing the transformation of the compliance function**, building on the work of her predecessor to reinforce expertise across all domains of non-compliance risk.
- **Contributing to the Group's strategic plan** — CEO Jean-Laurent Bonnafé expressed confidence in her ability to "continue the compliance function's transformation and thus contribute, alongside the businesses of the Group, to the success of our GTS 2025 plan."
- **Reporting to the General Management** — the compliance function sits directly under the CEO and General Management structure of BNP Paribas.

### Position in Governance

As of the 2024 integrated report, Stéphanie Maarek is listed as **Head of Compliance** on the BNP Paribas Executive Committee, alongside the CEO, COOs, Deputy COOs, and other functional and business heads.

## Philippe Maillard — Role and Responsibilities at BNP Paribas

**Current role:** Philippe Maillard serves as **Group Chief Operating Officer (COO)** of BNP Paribas, effective 11 February 2025. He is a member of the Group's Executive Committee and reports to Jean-Laurent Bonnafé, Chief Executive Officer of BNP Paribas. He replaced Laurent David in this position.

### Key Responsibilities

As Group COO, Philippe Maillard is responsible for the **Technology & Operational Performance** perimeter, which includes:

- **IT Group** (Group Information Technology)
- **Group Data Office**
- **Facilities management**
- **Procurement**
- **Internal consulting**

He oversees the improvement of operational performance, the development of technological resources, and the strengthening of cross-functional collaboration across the Group's business lines. Several senior leaders report to him, including the Group Chief Information Officer and the Group Head of Human Resources.

### Career Background

Philippe Maillard is a long-standing BNP Paribas veteran, having joined the bank in **1992** as a credit analyst. His career within the Group includes:

- Various roles in **Structured Finance**
- Four years in **Inspection Générale** (internal audit)
- Business Manager — Energy, Commodities, Export & Project (New York)
- Deputy Head of Business Management — Structured Finance
- Global Head of Performance Management at CIB Finance
- CFO of Global Equities & Commodity Derivatives
- COO of BNP Paribas Arbitrage
- Chief of Staff to Yann Gérardin (2015)
- COO for the **Asia-Pacific region** (2018)
- COO of the entire **Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB) division** (2019)

### Education

Philippe Maillard is a graduate of **École des Ponts ParisTech** (École Nationale des Ponts et Chaussées) and **Sciences Po Paris** (Institut d'Études Politiques).
